title: Who may read it, and who is using it
desc: Audience versus surfaces, attaching to agents, and what the Used by tab protects you from.
learningGoal: Share a base to exactly the right audience and know what depends on it before changing anything.

steps.title: Two dials, and they answer different questions
steps.bodyMd:
A knowledge base has two settings that look alike and do completely different jobs. Mix them up and you either hand the salary scheme to the whole company, or wonder all afternoon why your base never appears in a picker.

Open a base and go to **Settings**.

**Where it can be used** — three switches: **Agents**, **Chat**, **Automations**. The hint says it plainly: *"This decides which pickers offer this knowledge base. It does not change who may read what is in it — that is below."*

**Who may see and use it** — **Personal**, **Entire organisation** or **Groups**. This is the access rule, and the server checks it on every question anyone asks.

At Van Dijk Groep, Mark's base **Personeelshandboek** is offered to agents and chat but not to automations — while the whole organisation may read it.

One limit: you cannot turn all three surfaces off. Bee Flow refuses with *"A knowledge base has to be usable somewhere. Pick another place first."*

steps.question: Sandra unticks **Agents** on her base Inkoopvoorwaarden. Inkoopassistent — the purchasing agent her colleague Marloes built in the previous course — already links that base. What actually changes?

choices.label: The base stops being offered in agent pickers, but Marloes's Inkoopassistent keeps answering from it.
Everyone in the Inkoop group loses read access to the base.
choices.feedback: Read access lives in the block below, Who may see and use it. A surface switch is not a permission, and unticking one takes nothing away from a reader.

choices.label: The base is detached from every agent that links it.
choices.feedback: Nothing is detached. The base id stays in Marloes's agent configuration; it simply is not offered again in the picker.

choices.label: Nothing changes anywhere — the switch is a label only.
choices.feedback: It does bite: new links are refused, and the next time somebody saves an agent that still lists the base the save comes back with "not available for agents".

steps.explanation: Where it can be used steers pickers and new links. Who may read it is a separate, server-enforced rule — and the switch admits it: an unticked surface that still has links carries the amber note "still attached to {n}". Note who is who: the base is Sandra's, the agent is Marloes's, so a switch on your own base lands in someone else's agent — which is exactly what the Used by tab, later in this lesson, is for.

steps.title: Personal, the whole organisation, or named groups
steps.bodyMd:
Three rows, one choice.

- **Personal** — only you.
- **Entire organisation** — everybody at Van Dijk Groep.
- **Groups** — the row (or the **+**) opens the organisation's group list; the ones you tick appear as chips such as *Inkoop* or *Sales*. Picking the row alone shares nothing: the first ticked group does that, and unticking the last chip returns you to Personal.

Widening asks first — **"Share more widely?"**, with the buttons **Share** and **Keep as is**. Narrowing never asks.

A base built outside an organisation reads **"Personal — only you can see this"** and offers **Move to my organisation**. That move shares nothing by itself, but administrators gain the right to manage it, and there is no way back.

steps.title: A meeting tag widens who can read a summary
steps.bodyMd:
Ilse adds a **Meeting notes** source on the tag `sales`. The form says the consequence before she clicks: *"Everyone who can see this knowledge base will be able to read these summaries — including people who cannot open the meetings themselves. Transcripts never go in."*

So the meeting's own sharing stops mattering; the base's audience takes over. Under **What goes in**, **Summary** is always included and cannot be unticked, and **Decisions** arrives ticked as well; **Open questions** and **Actions** are yours to add.

One guardrail: the source reads meetings as the base's **owner**, so it can never pull in a meeting that owner could not open anyway. It widens the readers, never the reach.

steps.title: Give each base its audience
steps.instruction: Four knowledge bases at Van Dijk Groep. Pair each one with the audience you would set under Who may see and use it.

pairs.left: Personeelshandboek — the handbook, the leave policy and the expenses scheme that everybody asks about
pairs.note: Anyone may ask; nothing in it is narrower than the company itself.

pairs.left: Inkoopvoorwaarden — supplier framework agreements and the price arrangements behind them
pairs.note: Price arrangements are not company-wide reading. Share with the group that negotiates them.

pairs.left: Offertes & klantafspraken — meeting summaries pulled in by the tag sales
pairs.note: A meeting source hands its summaries to everyone who can see the base, so keep the base as narrow as the meetings were.

pairs.left: Mark's rough notes while he rewrites the leave policy — nothing agreed yet
pairs.note: Working notes get quoted back as fact with a citation. Keep them personal until they are finished.

steps.title: Your turn: write the handover note
steps.instruction: Ilse's base Offertes & klantafspraken is currently shared with Entire organisation, and she is about to add a Meeting notes source on the tag sales. Write two or three sentences for the colleague who takes this over. Say which audience you would set and why, name the consequence the meeting source warns about, and say which check you would do before saving the source with **Decisions** left ticked.
steps.placeholder: e.g. Before adding the tag I would narrow the audience from Entire organisation to the group Sales, because …

steps.title: Linking the base to an agent
steps.bodyMd:
Studio → **Agents** → your agent → tab **Can use** → the **Knowledge** card, subtitled *"Where it looks before it answers"* → **Link**. A panel lists **Knowledge bases**; every row carries **+ Link**, and one already attached reads **✓ Linked**. Only bases whose **Agents** switch is on are offered here. An agent with nothing linked says so: *"Nothing linked yet — this agent answers from its instructions alone."*

Then prove it: ask the agent the same question you used on the base's **Test question** tab, and check that the answer leans on the same documents. An agent searches every base it has linked at once, so a surprising answer may come from another base rather than a broken link.

Whether the answer prints its sources is an agent setting, not a base setting: **Include source references**, in the Knowledge card's ⋯ menu.

steps.title: Used by is the tab you read before you change anything
steps.bodyMd:
The base's fourth tab, **Used by**, carries a count and lists what references it — agents, skills, automations, apps, webpages, projects and notebooks — under the columns **Where**, **Does**, **Last time** and **Open**. Empty reads: *"No agent, skill or automation uses this knowledge base yet."*

Two readings to get right:

- A row you are not allowed to see keeps its kind and loses its name — **Someone else's agent**. It still counts.
- If a kind could not be checked, the **Delete this knowledge base** card in Settings says *"This list may be incomplete — … could not be checked."* That is not the same sentence as "nothing depends on this", and it should stop your hand.

steps.question: Sandra deletes the **Uploaded files** source — the one bucket that took her first five PDFs and the seven supplier agreements she added a week later. The dialog says: "Its 12 documents leave this knowledge base. The original files stay where they are." What follows from that?

choices.label: All 12 documents go with the source — every upload joined the same bucket — so answers can no longer quote them, while the files she uploaded still exist where they came from.
The documents stay in the base; only the connection to the source disappears.
choices.feedback: The documents belong to the source. When it goes they go, and every citation pointing at them dies with them.

choices.label: The original files are deleted as well.
choices.feedback: The dialog says the opposite in so many words: the original files stay where they are. Bee Flow removes its copy of the text, not your document.

choices.label: The whole knowledge base is removed.
choices.feedback: That is a different, deliberately separate button — Delete this knowledge base, in Settings, which warns that its documents go with it.

steps.explanation: Deleting a source is a content decision, not a tidy-up: its documents leave and any answer that used to cite them stops being able to. Check Used by first, so you know which agents get a thinner answer tomorrow.

steps.title: Link your base to an agent — we will verify it
steps.instruction: Open one of your own agents, go to the Can use tab, and use Link on the Knowledge card to attach a knowledge base you own. Save the agent. Then go back to the base and open its Used by tab: the agent should be listed there.

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- Set **Who may see and use it** deliberately — Personal, Entire organisation or a named group — and keep it separate in your head from **Where it can be used**, which only steers the pickers.
- Read a source's consequence line before you add it. A meeting tag hands its summaries to everyone who can see the base, whatever the meeting's own sharing said.
- Open **Used by** before you delete a source, retire a base or narrow its audience, and treat "could not be checked" as a reason to look again rather than a green light.

Next time an answer looks wrong, you now have two questions instead of one: is the content there, and is this person allowed to see it?

ex-knowledge-audience-note.title: Audience decision for a meeting-fed base
ex-knowledge-audience-note.task: Write two or three sentences of handover: which audience to set on a base that is about to receive a Meeting notes source on the tag sales, why, the consequence the meeting source warns about, and one check to do before saving the source with Decisions left ticked.
criteria: Names a concrete audience and narrows it — the group Sales rather than Entire organisation — with a reason tied to who should read sales meeting summaries.
States the consequence correctly: everyone who can see the knowledge base can read those summaries, including people who cannot open the meetings themselves.
Mentions a real check before saving the source with Decisions ticked, such as reading what the tagged meetings actually contain, or checking Used by / which agents already use the base.
Keeps audience (who may read) separate from surfaces (where it is offered) and does not present a surface switch as a permission.
ex-knowledge-audience-note.guidance: Do not pass an answer that only says "share it with the team" without naming the narrowing, nor one that claims the meeting's own sharing still protects the summaries, nor one that says unticking Agents or Chat keeps people out. An answer that mentions transcripts being excluded is correct but is not by itself enough.

practiceTopic.title: Knowledge base audience and dependencies
practiceTopic.summary: How a knowledge base decides who may read it, where it is offered, and what the Used by tab reveals before you change anything.
facts: The Settings tab has two separate blocks: "Where it can be used" (Agents, Chat, Automations) and "Who may see and use it" (Personal, Entire organisation, Groups).
The hint under Where it can be used says it decides which pickers offer the base and does not change who may read what is in it.
Turning off the last surface is refused with "A knowledge base has to be usable somewhere. Pick another place first."
Widening an audience asks "Share more widely?" with the buttons Share and Keep as is; narrowing does not ask.
A base with no organisation shows "Personal — only you can see this" and Move to my organisation, which cannot be undone and gives administrators management rights.
The Meeting notes source warns that everyone who can see the knowledge base can read those summaries, including people who cannot open the meetings, and that transcripts never go in.
Deleting a source shows "Its {count} documents leave this knowledge base. The original files stay where they are."

The Used by tab lists what references the base — agents, skills, automations, apps, webpages, projects and notebooks — under Where, Does, Last time and Open; rows you may not see keep their kind but lose their name ("Someone else's {kind}").

actionChecks.label: Attach a knowledge base to an agent
actionChecks.hint: In Studio → Agents → your agent → Can use → Knowledge → Link, then save the agent.

endpoints.returns: array of knowledge base rows the caller can see, each with id, name, tenant_id (owner user id), organization_id, usage_contexts

criteria.label: An agent uses one of your knowledge bases
criteria.hint: Open the base's Used by tab — the agent should be listed there.
criteria.rule: for at least one row of GET /api/kb whose tenant_id is the learner, GET /api/kb/:id/usage returns a usage row with kind === 'agent'
